question.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 5 & 1 & -11 & 15 \\  & ↓ & 5 & -30 \\  & 1 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-11x+15}{x-5}=x-6-\frac{15}{x-5}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{{x}^{2}-11x+15}{x-5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(x-6-\frac{15}{x-5})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x-6{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x-15{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{x-5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{4}-6x\,{|}_{0}^{4}-15\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-5|\,{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({4}^{2}-{0}^{2})-6(4-0)-15(\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-5|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-5|) \\  & =8-24-15(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡5) \\  & =15\operatorname{ln}⁡5-16.\end{aligned}
$$
